sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 12.8% a year, from $4.86 billion in FY2016 to $14.3 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F198].

FY2021 was the step change: revenue rose 89.1% to $16.1 billion, with REGEN-COV U.S. sales of $5.83 billion adding 66.4pp under a September 2021 U.S. government supply agreement [D241][F6][S48][D582][P39].
Revenue then fell 24.3% to $12.2 billion in FY2022 because REGEN-COV U.S. sales, $0 that year, did not recur [D292][F7][S49][P33].
Growth has slowed since: the FY2022 to FY2025 revenue CAGR is 5.6%, and FY2025 growth was 1.0% [D767][D440].
In FY2025 net product sales fell 17.3%, subtracting 9.3pp from growth, while collaboration revenue rose 21.0%, adding 9.0pp [D506][D507][D522][D523].
U.S. EYLEA sales fell 42.4% to $2.75 billion, a 14.2pp drag, on lower volumes, competition, compounded bevacizumab, the shift to EYLEA HD and a lower net price [S43][D577][D578][P10].
Regeneron's share of Sanofi antibody profits rose 33.6% to $5.24 billion, 36.5% of revenue, driven mainly by higher Dupixent sales [S52][D591][D590][P9].
Revenue growth of 1.0% ran 4.4pp below operating-cost growth in FY2025, and operating income fell 10.3% [D440][D464][D441].
Diluted EPS grew 8.2% against net income growth of 2.1%, because the diluted share count fell 5.6% [D444][D442][D459].
Operating margin of 24.9% in FY2025 is the window low, against a median of 34.6% and a high of 55.7% [F30][D749][D751][D750].
In FY2025 R&D cost 4.7pp of margin as R&D grew 14.0%, while SG&A added 2.0pp [D465][D455][D466].
SG&A fell mainly on lower charitable contributions to Good Days, a patient assistance organization [D466][P5].
The largest move was FY2022, down 16.7pp, with R&D costing 11.4pp and SG&A 6.0pp, the latter on higher headcount and Libtayo commercialization costs [D305][D318][D319][P34].
Net margin of 31.4% sits above operating margin of 24.9%, with other income of $1.65 billion in FY2025 [F50][F30][X117].
FY2025 operating cash flow of $4.98 billion was 1.11x net income, while free cash flow of $4.08 billion was 0.91x [F80][D428][F100][D429].
Free cash flow margin of 28.4% is above the window median of 26.4% [D425][D757].
Capex of $898 million was 6.3% of revenue and 1.65x D&A, after growing 18.9% [F90][D424][D430][D447].
Free cash flow to net income of 0.91x ranks in the 29th percentile of seven peers, whose median is 1.11x [D429][D782][D783].
Net cash reached $16.9 billion in FY2025, up from $15.9 billion, equal to 117.7% of revenue [D434][D385][D435].
That ranks in the 100th percentile of eight biopharma peers, whose median net cash is -50.7% of revenue [D780][D781].
The current ratio of 4.13x compares with its own window median of 3.97x [F180][D766].
Buybacks of $3.44 billion and dividends of $370 million took 93.3% of free cash flow, against 71.0% in FY2024 [X137][X140][D437][D388].
The diluted share count fell 5.6% to 108.6 million shares [D459][X127].
Operating margin fell four years in a row, 30.7pp in total, from 55.7% to 24.9% [R1][F26][F30].
R&D rose from 18.1% to 40.8% of revenue, and the FY2023 increase was partly due to the Sanofi amendments [D758][D420][D357][P24].
U.S. EYLEA sales have fallen three years running, by 8.7%, 16.7% and 42.4%, leaving 19.2% of revenue against 63.0% in FY2017 [D571][D574][D577][D576][D554].
Other income of $1.65 billion in FY2025 compares with $789 million in FY2024, and the cited filings do not explain the rise [X117][X116].
Data quality: the table's FY2018 revenue of $5.15 billion and FY2019 revenue of $6.56 billion are recasts of $6.71 billion and $7.86 billion first reported [R2][F3][X3][F4][X4].
I draw no conclusion from growth or margin comparisons across FY2018 and FY2019, and the CAGRs use unaffected endpoints [F198].
Operating margin below the 24.9% window low would confirm the compression trend, and a move above it would reverse it; see the FY2026 10-K [D749][F30].
U.S. EYLEA HD and EYLEA sales below the FY2025 level of $4.38 billion would confirm the erosion, and sales above it would reverse it; see the FY2026 10-K [S46].
Buybacks plus dividends above the FY2025 level of 93.3% of free cash flow would show returns outrunning cash generation; see the FY2026 10-K [D437].
